topic.topic: Ten percent a year for 50 years
topic.angle: Compound growth, as a number to feel

card.title: What does 10% a year do over 50 years?

body.question: If $1 grows by 10% every year for 50 years, about how many dollars does it become?
body.reveal: About $117. Growth that compounds, 1.10 multiplied by itself 50 times, is far bigger than the $6 you'd have if you added 10 cents of the original dollar each year. This is a maths example, not investment advice.

claims.claim: $1 at 10% compounded for 50 years is about $117
Compounding means 1.10 multiplied by itself 50 times
Simple growth (10% of original dollar each year) gives "5 times"
claims.quote: previously accumulated interest is not added to the principal amount of the current period
claims.note: Adding 10 cents a year for 50 years gives $1 + $5 = $6 total (6 times); the growth added is $5. Suggested: "far bigger than the $6 you'd get by adding 10 cents of the original dollar each year". Verified by calculation.

claims.quote: interest accumulated from a principal sum and previously accumulated interest
